name: Haloperidol
executiveSummary: Typical butyrophenone antipsychotic. Adult agitation: **0.5–5 mg PO/IM** (repeat q30–60 min; usual max **20 mg/day**). Chronic PO: **1–15 mg/day**. Nausea/palliative: **0.5–2 mg** q6–8h. IV: diluted/monitored only (QT). High EPS risk.
indications:
## Indications

- Psychosis/agitation; delirium (low doses); refractory nausea; chorea (regimens); Tourette syndrome.

## Precautions

- EPS, acute dystonia (treat with biperiden/diphenhydramine); NMS.
- QT — avoid other QT+; ECG if at risk.
- Dementia: ↑ mortality. Parkinson: avoid or minimal dose.

> Decanoate IM depot for specialist maintenance only.

adulto.presentation: Tabs 0.5–1–5–10 mg; drops; ampoule 5 mg/mL; decanoate depot.
adulto.dose: Agitation: **0.5–2 mg** (elderly) up to **5 mg** IM/PO; repeat by response (max ~**20 mg/day**). Psychosis: **1–15 mg/day** PO divided. Palliative/nausea: **0.5–1 mg** q8h. IV (ICU): **0.5–2 mg** slow — protocol.
adulto.administration: PO/IM. IV only with monitoring. Depot gluteal per label.

pediatrico.dose: Psychiatry: guide **0.025–0.05 mg/kg/day** divided (max by age) — specialist. Agitation: low one-off doses.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

EPS, akathisia, sedation, hyperprolactinemia, long QT; rare: NMS, seizures.
